## Setup

```{r}
#| label: setup

library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(broom)
library(ggtext)
library(scales)

TDS_BLUE  <- "#1b6ca8"
TDS_GOLD  <- "#c8a415"
TDS_DARK  <- "#1a1a2e"
TDS_RED   <- "#c0392b"
TDS_LIGHT <- "#f8f9fa"

theme_set(theme_light(base_size = 14))
```

## Load Data

```{r}
#| label: load-data

base_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2025/2025-04-22"

daily_accidents     <- read_csv(file.path(base_url, "daily_accidents.csv"))
daily_accidents_420 <- read_csv(file.path(base_url, "daily_accidents_420.csv"))
```

## The Hero Chart

::: callout-tip
## Design Brief

One chart. At 1200×628 (16:9 social ratio). No axis label that needs explaining. A viewer scrolling Instagram at speed should understand the finding in under 3 seconds. The title IS the finding.
:::

```{r}
#| label: hero-chart
#| fig-width: 12.5
#| fig-height: 6.54

holiday_data <- daily_accidents |>
  mutate(
    year      = year(date),
    wday      = wday(date, label = TRUE),
    month_day = format(date, "%m-%d"),
    holiday   = case_when(
      month_day == "07-04" ~ "July 4th",
      month_day == "07-03" ~ "July 3rd",
      month_day == "01-01" ~ "New Year's Day",
      month_day == "12-31" ~ "New Year's Eve",
      month_day == "12-23" ~ "Dec 23rd",
      month_day == "04-20" ~ "4/20",
      TRUE                 ~ "Baseline"
    ),
    holiday = fct_relevel(holiday, "Baseline")
  )

model_holidays <- lm(
  fatalities_count ~ holiday + year + wday,
  data = holiday_data
)

coef_data <- tidy(model_holidays, conf.int = TRUE) |>
  filter(str_detect(term, "^holiday")) |>
  mutate(
    term   = str_remove(term, "^holiday"),
    term   = fct_reorder(term, estimate),
    is_420 = term == "4/20",
    significant = !(conf.low < 0 & conf.high > 0)
  )

coef_data |>
  ggplot(aes(estimate, term)) +
  geom_rect(
    xmin = -Inf, xmax = 0, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
    fill = "#f5f5f5", alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_errorbarh(
    aes(xmin = conf.low, xmax = conf.high,
        colour = significant),
    height = 0.3, linewidth = 1
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(colour = significant, size = is_420)
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c("TRUE" = TDS_RED, "FALSE" = "grey60"),
    guide  = "none"
  ) +
  scale_size_manual(values = c("FALSE" = 3, "TRUE" = 5), guide = "none") +
  annotate(
    "text", x = -2, y = "4/20",
    label = "← no effect",
    colour = "grey50", size = 4, fontface = "italic", hjust = 1
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text", x = 22, y = "July 4th",
    label = "the real danger →",
    colour = TDS_RED, size = 4, fontface = "bold", hjust = 0
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "4/20 is not a dangerous day. July 4th is.",
    subtitle = "Extra fatalities per day vs. baseline, controlling for year and day of week | FARS 1992–2016",
    x        = "Additional fatalities above a typical day",
    y        = NULL,
    caption  = "TheDataShrink™ | Data: Harper & Palayew (2019) via TidyTuesday 2025-04-22"
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", size = 20, colour = TDS_DARK),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 13, colour = "grey40"),
    plot.caption  = element_text(size = 10, colour = "grey60"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

ggsave(
  "hero_fatal_car_crashes_on_4_20.png",
  width = 12.5, height = 6.54, dpi = 150
)
```

::: callout-note
## Why This Chart Works

-   The title is the finding — you don't need to read the axes
-   Red = significant effect, grey = not significant — one visual encoding, no legend needed
-   The annotation "← no effect" points directly at 4/20 so even a fast scroll reader gets it
-   July 4th sits clearly to the right — the contrast is immediate
:::

## Instagram Carousel Copy

::: callout-tip
## 5-Slide Structure: Hook → Data → Insight → Method → CTA
:::

**Slide 1 — Hook** *(full bleed, bold text on dark background)* \> "A 2018 study said 4/20 causes more fatal car crashes. \> A 2019 study proved them wrong. \> Here's what the data actually shows. 🧵"

------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Slide 2 — Data** *(show the calendar chart from H1)* \> "25 years of US fatal crash data. \> 1992 to 2016. Every single day. \> One date was supposed to stand out."

------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Slide 3 — Insight** *(hero chart, cropped to the key comparison)* \> "It doesn't. \> After controlling for year trends and day of week — \> 4/20 adds zero extra fatalities. \> July 4th adds 20."

------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Slide 4 — Method** *(code snippet or coefficient plot)* \> "The original paper compared 4/20 to a narrow window of nearby days. \> No trend adjustment. No day-of-week control. \> Change those two things — the effect disappears."

------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Slide 5 — CTA** \> "Full analysis with code on YouTube 👆 \> Built in R with tidyverse + broom + rsample. \> Follow @thedatashrink for weekly data stories. 📊"

## Facebook Post Template

```         
📊 Did 4/20 really cause more car crashes? A 2018 paper said yes.
A 2019 reanalysis said: not even close.

Here is what 25 years of US fatality data shows:

✅ July 4th: ~20 extra deaths above a typical day
✅ New Year's Eve: clearly elevated
✅ Dec 23rd: elevated (pre-Christmas travel)
❌ 4/20: statistically indistinguishable from any other April evening

The original paper's effect disappeared the moment you controlled
for the long-term decline in traffic fatalities and day of week.

Full analysis + code:
https://thedatashrink.com.au/tidytuesday/fatal_car_crashes_on_4_20

#DataScience #RStats #TidyTuesday #TheDataShrink #DataLiteracy
```

## Interactive Element (Shiny)

```{r}
#| label: interactive
#| eval: false

library(shiny)

# Minimal Shiny: pick any calendar date, see how it compares to the annual baseline
ui <- fluidPage(
  titlePanel("How dangerous is your birthday?"),
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      dateInput("date", "Pick a date (month + day used):",
                value = "2000-04-20",
                format = "mm-dd")
    ),
    mainPanel(plotOutput("comparison"))
  )
)

server <- function(input, output) {
  output$comparison <- renderPlot({
    target_md <- format(as.Date(input$date), "%m-%d")

    daily_accidents |>
      mutate(
        month_day = format(date, "%m-%d"),
        group     = if_else(month_day == target_md,
                            paste0("Your date (", target_md, ")"),
                            "All other days")
      ) |>
      ggplot(aes(group, fatalities_count, fill = group)) +
      geom_boxplot(show.legend = FALSE) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = c("All other days" = TDS_BLUE,
                                   paste0("Your date (", target_md, ")") = TDS_GOLD)) +
      labs(title = paste("Fatalities on", target_md, "vs. every other day"),
           x = NULL, y = "Daily fatalities") +
      theme_light(base_size = 14)
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```
